{"summary":"Read-only accessibility and interaction review completed against README.md, docs/MSW-CHEATSHEET.md, and bin/msw, grounded in Apple’s current [macOS guidance](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-macos/), [accessibility guidance](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility/), [MenuBarExtra window style](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/menubarextrastyle/window), and [String Catalog guidance](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/localizing-and-varying-text-with-a-string-catalog).

Checklist and UI decisions:
[ ] Use MenuBarExtra with .menuBarExtraStyle(.window), because lifecycle controls, forms, and progress need window-style interaction. Keep a stable monochrome SF Symbol in the menu bar; switch to an exclamation badge only for actionable failures. Give it the VoiceOver label “MicroSandbox Workspaces” and value such as “2 running, 1 stopped.”
[ ] Start near 400 × 560 points, allow approximately 360–480 width and 420–680 height, constrain to the screen’s visible frame, and scroll content instead of clipping it. Open logs, live metrics, disk details, backup history, and GitHub workflows in separate resizable windows, initially about 760 × 520 points.
[ ] Present the three workspaces in a List(selection:) with status text; keep row selection separate from actions. Put actions for the selected workspace below in labeled Sections. Use native Button, Label, ControlGroup, Menu, Picker, TextField, SecureField, Toggle, LabeledContent, Table, ProgressView, alert, and confirmationDialog controls; avoid clickable HStacks, gesture-only controls, and icon-only custom buttons.
[ ] Use distinct Start, Stop, and Restart buttons rather than a toggle. Disable actions that cannot currently run and explain why with .help. While an operation runs, disable conflicting actions and show “Starting dev,” “Stopping dev,” or “Restarting dev” in a labeled ProgressView. Popover dismissal must not cancel the process.
[ ] Change benign auto-starting commands to explicit labels when stopped: “Start and Open Website,” “Start and Open in Zed,” and “Start and Open Shell.” Use a validated integer port TextField, HTTP/HTTPS Picker, and remote-path TextField with recent-path suggestions. Keep Start, single-workspace Stop, and single-workspace Restart immediate; confirm Stop All or Restart All.
[ ] Show metrics and disk as exact localized values in LabeledContent/Table rows, optionally supplemented by gauges. Charts must have textual summaries. Disk inspection currently starts a stopped workspace, so label that action “Start and Show Disk.”
[ ] Put logs in a separate window with selectable monospaced text, search, source/level filters, Pause/Resume, Follow, and “Clear Display.” Do not announce every incoming line or move focus during streaming; expose a concise value such as “24 new lines” and a “Jump to Latest” action.
[ ] Make Backup a dedicated preflight view showing destination, estimated scope, and which running workspaces will temporarily stop. “Back Up Now” needs no alert after this explicit review surface. Show phase-based ProgressView feedback and, on success, archive/checksum paths plus “Reveal in Finder.” Only offer Cancel if cleanup and workspace restart remain safe.
[ ] Treat Restore as destructive: verify the archive first, summarize replacement scope, rollback location, unchanged Keychain tokens, and the fact that workspaces remain stopped. Use a confirmation dialog with “Cancel” as the default and “Restore Backup” as the destructive action. Keep the completion result visible with the required repair/check next steps.
[ ] Use a GitHub setup form with OWNER/REPOSITORY validation, access-mode Picker, and SecureFields for tokens; never echo, persist in view history, logs, or accessibility values. Show verification phases. Confirm credential removal with a destructive “Remove GitHub Access” action.
[ ] Always present Push in a review sheet containing workspace, repository, path, branch, commit, mode, and commits. Default to Cancel; the affirmative button is “Push.” Block non-fast-forward pushes, then expose a separate “Force with Lease…” flow with a second target-specific destructive confirmation. Never use a generic Yes button.
[ ] Encode status with text + shape + semantic color: “Running” with play/check symbol and green; “Stopped” with stop symbol and secondary color; “Starting/Restarting” with ProgressView and text; “Needs Attention” with warning triangle and red; “Quarantined” with lock/warning symbol and text. Use semantic system colors and SF Symbols, preserve contrast in light/dark and Increase Contrast modes, and respect Differentiate Without Color, Reduce Motion, and Reduce Transparency.
[ ] Let standard controls supply semantics. Combine children only for read-only status summaries, never groups containing buttons. Suggested labels include “Status, running,” “Start dev workspace,” “Open dev website on port 3000,” “Open dev in Zed,” “Open dev shell,” and “Push main branch of OWNER/REPOSITORY.” Use hints only for non-obvious consequences such as auto-starting or temporarily stopping workspaces; hide decorative symbols from accessibility.
[ ] Use @FocusState for keyboard focus. On opening, restore the prior selected workspace and focus the selected row or first available action. Maintain top-to-bottom tab order and native arrow-key behavior. Escape closes transient UI, Command-W closes secondary windows, and focus returns to the invoking control. Do not move focus for polling updates; use @AccessibilityFocusState only to move VoiceOver to the first invalid field, a blocking error, or a single completion summary.
[ ] Provide Command-R Refresh, Command-O Open Website, Command-L Show Logs, Command-comma Settings, Command-question-mark Help, and Command-Q Quit through SwiftUI Commands/keyboardShortcut. Show them in menus and tooltips and disable them when invalid. Do not assign direct shortcuts to Stop, Restart, Push, Force Push, credential removal, or Restore.
[ ] Show validation errors inline beside their field. Use a persistent Label-based error banner for command failures with a plain-language title, sanitized cause, recovery action, Retry, Copy Diagnostics, and Show Logs. Reserve alerts for blocking states and high-impact confirmation. Show successful routine actions inline rather than in modal alerts; optionally send a quiet notification only when a long operation finishes while its window is closed.
[ ] Put every user-facing label, hint, status, error, menu command, and notification in Localizable.xcstrings using LocalizedStringResource and translator comments. Avoid sentence concatenation; add plural variants. Format byte counts, percentages, dates, times, and durations with locale-aware FormatStyle APIs. Keep workspace names, paths, URLs, Git refs, hashes, and log output verbatim data rather than translating them.
[ ] Use leading/trailing alignment and native layouts so RTL interfaces mirror automatically. Keep terminal/log/path content in its natural text direction and protect mixed-direction identifiers. Allow labels to wrap and test long German/French strings, Arabic/Hebrew RTL, CJK, VoiceOver, Voice Control, Full Keyboard Access, light/dark appearances, Increase Contrast, Differentiate Without Color, Reduce Motion, missing Zed/Keychain credentials, quarantined workspaces, slow/failing operations, cancellation, and popover closure during work.

Verification was read-only: relevant command behavior and safety boundaries were inspected, current Apple documentation was checked, and git status confirmed this review introduced no file changes. Per instruction, no project-wide tests, formatters, or linters were run.","filesChanged":[]}
